author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner list treats a page below one as the first page
summary: Opening the owner list at page zero or any lower page renders the error page today. The owner list must treat any page value below one as the first page and respond with the normal listing.
acceptance_criteria: given a request for the owner list with page=0, when it is opened, then the response is HTTP 200 and renders the owner list view, not the error page
given a request for the owner list with a negative page value, when it is opened, then the response is HTTP 200 and renders the owner list view, not the error page
given a page value below one, when the owner list renders, then it lists the same owners and shows the same current page as a request for page one
non_goals: Non-numeric page values: the intake names only page values below 1; their handling stays open
Page values beyond the last page: not named in the intake; stays open
Any change to page size or to the search behavior of REQ-OWN-002
notes: Owner intake quote (intake-decision line 1): 'the owner listing treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal listing (HTTP 200).' Observed cause for design triage: the listing converts the 1-based page to a zero-based page request with no lower bound, so a page value of 0 or lower yields an invalid page request; the mechanism choice belongs to system-design-expert. processFindFormTreatsPageBelowOneAsFirstPage is one data-driven test covering at least page=0 and one negative value (e.g. -1). docs/prd.md already carries the REQ-OWN-005 narrative, anchor, and Done-when bullet from this dispatch; no Non-Goals row changed.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Covered by architecture-principles § Pattern catalog, Web controller row: normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range is binding and belongs in the controller, not a business rule. system-design § Contracts OwnerController row (search with paging) owns it; REQ-OWN-005 now joins that row. Cause located by grep (weaker basis, no IDE oracle): OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName builds PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize), and PageRequest rejects a negative index, so page <= 0 throws and the error page renders. Fix: in processFindForm, clamp page to at least 1 once at method entry, before both the query and addPaginationModel, so currentPage matches a page=1 request (AC 3).
integration_points: Framework transport: MockMvc via the existing @WebMvcTest(OwnerController.class) harness (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy, the sanctioned transport stand-in); per testing-principles § Test pyramid, controller-assigned normalization is tested at the web level, not extracted for a unit test

Repository boundary (OwnerRepository): reuse the suite's existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository fixture, stubbing findByLastNameStartingWith to return a multi-owner PageImpl; the class-wide fixture already uses this stub and a real repository would need a full-context test for a pure binding fix. Assert the captured Pageable has page index 0, and that model attribute currentPage is 1
Binding: the entry point is unchanged. page stays an int @RequestParam (request-scoped scalar); Owner binding is unchanged and out of this slice's scope

patterns.ref: docs/architecture-principles.md § Pattern catalog, Web controller row
patterns.description: request-parameter range normalization is binding in the controller
existing paged owner-list MockMvc test to model processFindFormTreatsPageBelowOneAsFirstPage on (data-driven over 0 and -1)

risks.risk: Clamping only inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName would leave currentPage at 0 or below in the model, breaking AC 3 and the pager links
risks.mitigation: Normalize once at processFindForm entry and pass the normalized value to both helpers (architecture-principles Web controller row)

risks.risk: Owner-list query path scales with owner count; docs/system-design.md carries no § Scale and Load section to cite
risks.mitigation: This slice adds no new data-scaling path; the query stays fixed-size paged. Simplest readable form (a Math.max clamp) is the design

notes: No design-doc-autofix records to audit. Out of scope, recorded for the owner: VetController.findPaginated builds PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...) the same way, so /vets.html?page=0 very likely fails the same way; it is not in this slice (prd-entry file_targets and intake name only the owner list). Non-numeric and past-last-page values stay open per the prd-entry non_goals.

findings.description: theOwnerListShouldTreatAPageBelowOneAsTheFirstPage captures the Pageable argument with an ArgumentCaptor and asserts only its picked pageNumber field, even though PageRequest is a real value object with equals()/hashCode() and a whole expected object can be built (PageRequest.of(firstPageIndex, 5)). testing-principles.md's whole-object comparison rule (mirrored in the test-review checklist's Mocking Policy item) calls a captor-plus-field-access chain a finding when a whole-object comparison is available.
findings.fix: Replace the ArgumentCaptor and the trailing assertThat(...).isEqualTo(firstPageIndex) with a single verify(this.owners).findByLastNameStartingWith(anyString(), eq(PageRequest.of(firstPageIndex, 5))) using the whole PageRequest value object (org.springframework.data.domain.PageRequest is already imported transitively via Pageable; add the import). Drop the now-unused ArgumentCaptor import.

semantic_surprise.note: The only behavior change is Math.max(page, 1) at method entry, threaded into both the repository call and the currentPage model attribute; page 1 and higher behave exactly as before, and values below one that used to reach PageRequest.of with a negative index and fail now list page one.

test_adequacy.note: The parameterized MockMvc test covers page 0 and -1 and checks the real outcome at both ends: the repository receives PageRequest.of(0, 5) and the model shows currentPage 1. A clamp applied only to the model or only to the query would fail it.
